title: Every boot that resumes an open position drops the anti-rug WebSocket subscription: resume registers the position and then re-arms the chain listener, whose un-awaited off() and on() of the same filter race inside ethers, so the new dispatcher lands on a stopped subscriber and no eth_subscribe is sent

evidence.note: resumeAntiRugMonitoring step 3: registerAntiRugPosition for each open position, which calls startChainAntiRugListener (detector.ts:447) and installs the address filter
step 4: startChainAntiRugListener(ctx) again for every verified chain, with the same registered address set
a dispatcher is already installed, so ctx.wsProvider.off(state.activeFilter, state.activeDispatcher) is called and not awaited
then ctx.wsProvider.on(filter, dispatcher), also not awaited, with a filter of the same addresses and topics, so ethers computes the same subscription tag

evidence.ref: sed -n 1040,1160p node_modules/ethers/lib.commonjs/providers/abstract-provider.js (ethers 6.16.0, the version package-lock.json pins for node_modules/ethers)
evidence.note: on() and off() each await getSubscription before touching #subs; on() looks the tag up before off() deletes it, gets the old subscriber (already started, so nothing is started) and pushes the new listener onto it; off() then removes the old listener, finds none left, calls subscriber.stop() (eth_unsubscribe) and deletes the tag. Pure microtask order inside ethers, no network between, so a real node sees the same sequence
antirug.listener.subscribed is logged on both calls, so the log says the subscription was installed twice while none remains
startMultiChainBot calls resumeAntiRugMonitoring once at every boot; the same code at HEAD (src unchanged in Phase 23): bot.ts:1807, :2122, :2132-2146; detector.ts:450, :647, :658, :667

real ETH V2 snipe on a temp-file database, armed; an LP Transfer to an allowlisted locker is evaluated (antirug.allowlist-hit); after restartGraph and the real resumeMultiChainMonitoring and resumeAntiRugMonitoring: two antirug.listener.subscribed lines, one eth_subscribe for the pair then its eth_unsubscribe and no other, the node holds no logs subscription, and a second LP Transfer to another locker is never evaluated (claim resume-drops-ws-subscription); the position is still in getRegisteredPositions and its exit monitor is armed. Fix-shaped mutations (await the off(); skip an unchanged re-subscribe) each read looks fixed, detector.ts restored identical
first seen here: on base, after the restart that picks up the script's deliberate position, the queued eth_unsubscribe drained and the node held zero subscriptions

sibling_sites_checked: Every caller of startChainAntiRugListener at the base: registerAntiRugPosition (detector.ts:447), the reconnect path (:943) and boot step 4 (bot.ts:2144). Reconnect: the new provider has no subscriber under the old tag, so off() is a no-op on it and on() subscribes (not affected; the old provider is AUD-ANTIRUG-001). registerAntiRugPosition for a position on a pair that is NOT yet watched changes the address set, so the tag differs and on() creates a new subscriber (not affected). registerAntiRugPosition for a second position on a pair that IS already watched (bucket.push, :416-421) keeps the address set unchanged and takes the same off()/on() path: by code reading the same race drops the subscription for every watched pair (not run). After a drop, the next registration of a new pair restores the subscription with the full set, so the blind window is from boot to the next new-pair buy. The HTTP-polling fallback (no WS URL) does not use the filter subscription. bot.ts DEX listeners call on() once per start (not affected). Interaction: the interim operator rule on AUD-BUY-001 (ESC-BUY-01, restart the main bot after any deliberate buy) re-arms the exit monitor but, through this finding, not the anti-rug subscription.
severity_rationale: S1 (capital can be stranded under a plausible condition), STRAND, graded by the 23-06 executor under the operator's standing instruction of 2026-11-11 ("All the bugs are going to get fixed. The S1, 2 or whatever doesn't matter. Don't interrupt sessions to ask me about upgrading or downgrading"), without a stop. Condition: any boot with an open position on a chain that has a WebSocket URL, which is the ordinary restart. Effect: the position is registered, the dashboard shows it monitored and the log says the subscription was installed, but no rug log reaches the evaluator until a later buy on a new pair re-subscribes, so liquidity removal is not seen for as long as that takes. The exit monitor is not affected. Graded like AUD-ANTIRUG-001 (S1, STRAND: the rug-log subscription can vanish after a dashboard stop); anti-rug live execution defaults to dry-run, which limits what a delivered log would do today but not the grade, as for AUD-ANTIRUG-001.

traces.scenario: Boot with one open position on a WebSocket chain (ETH V2 in the proof)
steps: Step 3: registerAntiRugPosition adds the position and calls startChainAntiRugListener: no prior dispatcher, so on(F) subscribes (eth_subscribe for [pair]).
Step 4: startChainAntiRugListener again: a dispatcher exists, so off(F) then on(F') run without await; F and F' have the same tag.
Inside ethers, on(F') finds the existing subscriber and attaches the new dispatcher to it; off(F) then removes the old dispatcher, stops the subscriber (eth_unsubscribe) and deletes the tag.
No eth_subscribe follows; the node holds no subscription; LP Transfer and Burn logs on the pair are never delivered.
traces.outcome: Anti-rug is blind for every resumed position until a new pair is registered, while the registry, the dashboard and the logs show it armed.

recommendation: Phase 24 (capital fix, with card OD-11's single WebSocket owner if that lands first): await the off() before the on(), or skip the re-subscribe when the watched address set is unchanged, and assert the node-side subscription after boot (test/realpath/triage/AUD-ANTIRUG-025.test.ts reads looks fixed for both shapes). Until fixed, after any restart with open positions on a WebSocket chain the anti-rug subscription is not live; this weakens the interim rule on AUD-BUY-001 (restart the main bot after a deliberate buy). Nothing is fixed in Phase 23.

triage.note: Found by 23-06 while proving AUD-BUY-001; real ETH V2 snipe armed on a temp file, restartGraph, real resumeMultiChainMonitoring + resumeAntiRugMonitoring: the node holds no subscription for the pair and an LP transfer to an allowlisted locker is never evaluated (claim resume-drops-ws-subscription); before the restart the same transfer is evaluated; awaiting off() and skipping an unchanged re-subscribe each read looks fixed
